title: The Missing Second Manuscript: Phase X as Philological Reconstruction of the Lost Transition in Marx's Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 (EA-SEI-PHASEX-LACUNA-01 v1.1)
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
This paper reframes Phase X as a conjectural reconstruction constrained by the incomplete manuscript tradition of Marx’s 1844 notebooks. Its factual starting point is that only pages XL–XLIII of the Second Manuscript survive and that passages in the Third Manuscript explicitly refer back to missing pages XXXVI and XXXIX. The paper argues that the surviving architecture leaves an unresolved movement between communism as fully developed humanism and the subsequent critique of Hegel.

The work divides its evidence into four grades. Grade A covers physical manuscript and cross-reference facts. Grade B is architectural inference about what argumentative work the missing pages may have performed. Grade C is the author’s proposed reconstruction of that function. Grade D is a historical suppression hypothesis involving the manuscripts’ custody, the purge of David Riazanov, the succession of Vladimir Adoratsky, Stalinist editorial control, and later Soviet hostility to alienation theory.

The conjectural passage is explicitly not offered as Marx’s recovered wording. It proposes that material emancipation begins rather than ends conscious human history, that alienation of thought may persist after property relations change, and that critique must turn toward the symbolic and philosophical form of abstraction. The Phase X Invariance Condition is then labeled a theoretical extrapolation from the reconstruction: a society that changes material relations without transforming symbolic-linguistic infrastructure will reproduce alienation in thought and coordination.

The paper is strongest where it preserves the evidence grades and states falsifiers: discovery of the missing pages, evidence of earlier accidental loss, demonstration that no transition is missing, or a post-capitalist counterexample. Its SPXI claims that Phase X is “not a theoretical inference” overstate the body’s own method. The location of the lacuna and the text of the bridge are inferential; the proposed passage is original reconstruction, not lost Marx.

The suppression tier requires special caution. A politically charged custody history and documented later censorship do not prove that particular pages were deliberately removed or ever entered Soviet custody intact.

wiki_article:
**The Missing Second Manuscript** is a philological and theoretical paper by Lee Sharks about Marx’s incomplete 1844 manuscripts.

The paper begins from the survival of only four pages of the Second Manuscript and references in the Third Manuscript to pages that are missing. It argues that the gap may have contained an argumentative transition between communism-as-humanism and the critique of Hegel.

A proposed passage reconstructs the function of that transition, not Marx’s exact words. The paper separately grades a speculative Soviet-suppression hypothesis.

Phase X and its invariance condition are therefore conjectural reconstruction and theoretical extrapolation, not recovered manuscript text.
